requirements: Anther makes pollen; stigma receives pollen, neither is a gamete.
Stigma/style/ovary maintain orientation; introduce a nested inset for ovule, embryo sac and egg.
Ovary contains ovules; ovule contains embryo sac; egg is inside that sac. Containment is not a transformation.
Pollen grain differs from sperm cell. Stage landmarks and close-up labels instead of seven simultaneous labels on a small flower.
Pollen remains at stigma while a tube provides a route through style towards ovule.
Separately labelled sperm travels through the route to embryo sac and egg; the entire pollen grain does not become sperm or pass through the egg.
Show sperm-egg fusion forming a zygote as a cell inset, retaining the surrounding ovule.
Stop transfer, tube delivery and fusion at separately spoken cues; arrival alone is not completed fusion.
Zygote divides/develops into embryo; retain the embryo inside a seed boundary.
Surrounding ovule develops into seed, not into zygote; seed coat is not drawn as generated only by the zygote.
Ovary-to-fruit is separate and qualified usually.
State embryo-forming focus; omit endosperm consistently rather than displaying a second embryo or claiming a complete life cycle.
Runner is a stem from parent; node is a leaf/bud location.
Roots and shoot develop at a suitable node before a new plant can become independent.
No instantaneous detachment, stem-length-only reproduction or universal identical-clone label.
Use no-fusion as event criterion; mutation/resource/later-survival limits remain in exact speech.
Same-plant and different-plant pollen source/destination cases shown sequentially.
Fusion is a separate conditional step after compatible pollen, not a guaranteed result of a transfer arrow.
